comparator.name: Political Science track of Philosophy of a Specific Discipline
comparator.sourceNotes: The normalized registry target is a VARIANT of recognized programme 57084, not an independently specified Political Science bachelor. The current official degree page identifies 57084 as the English-taught BA Philosophy of a Specific Discipline and explicitly allocates 120 EC to a student's first bachelor plus 60 EC to philosophy. The faculty's 2026–27 track document confirms a named Political Science track and lists permitted advanced philosophy modules, but does not identify a particular student's first bachelor or specify its 120-EC component curriculum. The supported structural groups total 180 EC; the 120-EC group is an externally determined curriculum, not free elective space or a defined Groningen Political Science major. The prospectus indexes the current 2026–27 guide and track list. No unrelated political-science bachelor is substituted to fill this unknown portion.

components.name: Course units of the student's first bachelor
components.note: The official degree structure transfers 120 EC from a separate first BA; the named Political Science philosophy track does not specify that BA's individual courses.

components.name: Introductory philosophy minor
components.note: Six introductory philosophy courses across its historical and principal thematic areas; individual selections are not established here.

components.name: Philosophy specialisation course related to the first bachelor
components.note: The programme requires a course connecting philosophical study to the first BA discipline.

components.name: Three advanced philosophy electives
components.note: The 2026–27 Political Science list offers an approved selection of modules; these are choices rather than a single compulsory set.

components.name: Bachelor's thesis in philosophy of the first discipline
components.note: Independent philosophical research related to the student's first BA.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized variant explicitly names Political Science and the faculty's 2026–27 track list confirms that exact track. The route is therefore fixed by target identity; it is not chosen for UCR fit. Its track designation specifies philosophy elective context, but does not itself define the 120 EC supplied by the student's original bachelor.

programmes.label: Political Science track of Philosophy of a Specific Discipline at University of Groningen

exception.reason: The current official sources establish the Political Science philosophy track and its 60-EC philosophy structure, but 120 EC of the 180-EC degree comes from a separate first bachelor that is not identified or reconstructed for this normalized target. The track's elective list is not a 120-EC political-science curriculum. Replacing that portion with invented political-science courses or treating it as open elective space would produce a misleading comparator and invalid course-level alignment. A fixed comparison must wait until an authoritative first-BA pathway and its components can be identified, or the normalized target's presentation scope is resolved.
exception.curriculumContext: The supported degree structure is 120 EC credited from the first BA, 30 EC introductory philosophy, a 5-EC discipline-related philosophical specialisation, 15 EC chosen from advanced philosophy offerings and a 10-EC philosophy thesis. The 2026–27 Political Science list includes, among other options, feminist philosophy, consent, public institutions, democratic theory and global justice. These demonstrate the track's philosophical orientation but do not identify the first BA's 120 EC. No UCR alternatives or comparison blocks are asserted while that defining curriculum remains unresolved.
